t.5.39.1: And the monkey, honored by her with words of praise as he was about to depart, withdrew from that place and began to reflect.
t.5.39.2: Only a little of this task remains, for this dark-eyed lady has been seen. Passing over the three means, the fourth alone appears fitting here.
t.5.39.3: Conciliation does not serve any good purpose among rākṣasas, nor does a gift avail with those who are heaped with wealth; people proud of their strength cannot be won over by sowing dissension. Valour alone, therefore, is what pleases me here.
t.5.39.4: No resolution of this task can be reached here except through valour; for only when their foremost heroes have been slain in battle might the rākṣasas somehow come to softness here today.
t.5.39.6: Indeed, in this world there is no single means that accomplishes even a very small task; he who understands a purpose in its many ways is the one capable of achieving that purpose.
t.5.39.5: He who, when charged with a task that must be done, can accomplish many other things as well without conflicting with the original task, is truly fit to carry out the work.
t.5.39.7: Indeed, I have made up my mind right here: if I go to the abode of the lord of the monkeys only after learning the true measure of the difference between the enemy's strength and my own in a clash, then my master's command will have been fulfilled.
t.5.39.9: This excellent grove of that cruel one, like Nandana, pleasing to the eye and the mind, is filled with various trees and creepers.
t.5.39.8: How indeed might a happy chance arise for me today to force a battle with the rākṣasas, and likewise how might Daśānana bring his own mighty army, and me as well, together on the field of battle?
t.5.39.10: I shall destroy this grove as fire destroys a dry forest; and when it has been laid waste, that Rāvaṇa will then fall into a rage.
t.5.39.12: But I, of unimpeded valour, having met in battle those rākṣasas of fierce prowess and slain that army urged on by Rāvaṇa, shall go happily to the abode of the lord of the monkeys.
t.5.39.11: Then the lord of the rākṣasas will assemble a great army, with horses, mighty chariots and elephants, armed with tridents, iron weapons and paṭṭiśas, and then this great battle will take place.
t.5.39.13: Then Māruti, of terrible prowess, enraged like the wind, began to hurl down the trees with the mighty force of his thighs.
t.5.39.14: Then the heroic Hanumān destroyed that pleasure-grove of the women, which resounded with the cries of excited birds and was filled with various trees and creepers.
t.5.39.15: With its trees crushed, its pools of water shattered, and its mountain peaks ground to powder, that grove became unpleasant to behold.
t.5.39.16: With its bowers of creepers and its painted pavilions destroyed, its great serpents and beasts of prey driven off, and its stone houses and other dwellings torn apart, that great grove became one whose form was utterly ruined.
t.5.39.17: Having caused great distress to the mind of that mighty lord of riches, the great monkey, eager to fight alone against many of great strength, took his stand at the archway, blazing with splendour.
